item.title: Re: Couldn't help myself....
item.content:encoded:
Ok…I was thinking that it was only 150,000-200,000 years, that is why it brought the question to mind, as it would have made her one of the very first homo sapiens in existence (that is, assuming that she IS human. Who knows, she could only look human because a human is the one looking at her).

I got 260,000 too, when I did the math, but decided to round down to the nearest 100k, because I wasn't sure that I had it right. That's why qualified it as "around 200,000". Going with your numbers though, that still puts her outside the "accepted" range of when homo sapiens existed.
In the note for 1/3/49, it mentions thought that she nodded….I would think that if they had a good enough image to notice such a slight movement, then with modern optics and means, they would be able to tell the difference between a Homo Sapiens Sapiens and Homo Florensis, as, while at first glance they do look similar, there are marked differences in facial and body structure.

I hadn't thought of her, basically, getting bored and just listening in on broadcasts from Earth. That would explain it though.

For my interpretation….well, I had a few ideas. Reading it, the first thought that popped into my head was the Primordial Nyx (Nox)….I just couldn't come up with any reason she would be doing what she does. I had a few others, mostly based around some sort of alchemical process…but the one I'm kind of settling on, for the moment at least, is a reality bender that for some reason has taken it upon herself to be a "watcher of earth".

item.title: Re: Couldn't help myself....
item.content:encoded:
Modern Human i.e. Homo Sapiens Sapiens have been around since 250,000 years ago, IIRC, and previous human species have been here for couple million years—there are notable differences, but without comparison out there in outer space, Homo Florensis would look exactly like normal human. Also, this thing could "hear" electromagnetic radiations, I think listening to earth radio isn't really difficult for it.

the hair was 34 km long, btw, which with 15 cm/year average would put it on around 227,000 years old. 39 km hair would put its age on exactly 260,000 y.o.

Of course, you're free to have your own interpretation about what /exactly/ is this thing!

item.title: Couldn't help myself....
item.content:encoded:
I got started thinking about how old she was, so I couldn't help myself…I had to figure it out.
(the math here is based on a few assumptions and averages so it will, of course, be off by a few years.)

Since she appears human, I am taking that as a base.

Human hair grows at an average of 15 cm/year
Assuming that her hair had never been cut, with her hair being 39 km, that puts her age at around 200,000 years old, if I did the math right.

Not sure why it bugged me, until I figured it out, but there you have it.

Of course this leads to another question….how was there someone recognizably human, by modern standards, around 200,000 years ago? (And how did she learn modern french?)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like this SCP. She doesn't want to be trapped by the Foundation because they inevitably will try to restrict movement or cordon off others from interacting with the SCP. The SCP wants to just exist and do her job, whatever it is, and no one possesses, or should possess, the knowledge and power she has because to do so would be anathema to her existence - her whole existence is to be a free agent and to do the right thing (or rather, its duty) without smaller beings' agendas interfering, even if they may align with each other on many points.

It's the SCP's instinct to understand, know, monitor, and, if possible, keep these things secret from the ignorant populace and people who may want to use SCPs for evil, but she seems to be literally above it all. Giving little to no information to no one averts the possibility of her freedom being compromised by anyone or anything, in theory.

I don't know, I really, really dug this SCP and the implications that, despite science's overall objective
being to understand and explain certain phenomena and the unknown, there are some things that shouldn't be left alone, necessarily, but our attempts to reel them in are laughably limited and negligible and in this case it's probably for the best. Her staying in the sky is perhaps how she's able to see everything. If she's wrangled or sequestered in the sky somehow, she may become somewhat blind to or not be able to perceive dangerous undercurrents in our universe and in other universes.

From the Object Classes Guide:

Thaumiel-class objects are highly classified and extremely rare anomalies that are utilized by the Foundation to contain or counteract the effects of other highly dangerous anomalies, especially Keter-class objects. Even the mere existence of Thaumiel-class objects is classified at the highest levels of the Foundation and their locations, functions, and current status are known to few Foundation personnel outside of the O5 Council.

In-universe, SCPs are likely promoted to Thaumiel class or just classified that immediately by following these guidelines.

From a writer's perspective, they just write it as a Thaumiel. We don't actually change classifications in real-time edits.
